data.long_meaning: The one who brings the morning, the radiant one. The name Sabaha carries the meaning “Morning, Radiance” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Sabaha usually hope their child will grow to embody morning, radiance and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Sabaha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Morning, Radiance.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sabaha total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_english.name: Sabaha
in_english.meaning: Dawn, grief, the first day, beginning
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sabaha comes from the root Sabaha, which means the early morning, or the grief of the dead. In Islam, Sabaha is considered a permissible name for women, and it is believed to have a positive impact on the child. Sabaha is also a name that reminds us of the prophetic promise, as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said in a hadith: "Sabaha, people will grieve for it"

data.cultural_impact: The name Sabaha has a beautiful and poetic meaning in Arabic, which translates to "the one who brings the morning, the radiant one." This name is a reminder of the joy and fresh start that comes with each new day. In many Islamic cultures, the dawn prayer (Fajr Salah) is a significant part of daily worship, which reflects the importance of acknowledging and welcoming the arrival of a new day. Furthermore, the cyclical nature of the Arabic calendar, which is based on lunar cycles, also reinforces this focus on the start of new months and new beginnings. thus, the name Sabaha can be seen as a celebration of the beauty and renewal that each new day brings.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Sabaha carries deep spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. The idea of Sabah, or the light of dawn, is a recurring theme in Quranic verses that emphasize the importance of seeking knowledge, guidance, and renewal. For example, in Surah Al-Anfal (8:18), Allah says, "And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant [this Qur’an] with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear, we understand.' [Surely, the honor, the fate, and the life of every person lies in the hands of Allah]. And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is knowledgeable of that within the breasts."
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Morning, Radiance" symbolizes The one who brings the morning, the radiant one. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Sabaha serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of morning, radiance.
